data.narrative:
Dusty Robotics is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Tessa Lau and Philipp Herget. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private companies and 1 public company (277810.KQ) in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including peers such as Humanoid, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI at Series A and Series B stages.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using the company's $70M+ total raised as a proxy for Series A base value of $26M, applied a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for advancement to the next financing stage, implying a valuation of $52M. The peer-median method examined five same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $1.1B (Walden Robotics, Seed) to $2.0B (Generalist AI, Series B), yielding a median of $1.6B.

The two methods produce a wide implied range of $44M to $1.9B, with a triangulated median of $851M. The significant divergence reflects material uncertainty regarding whether Dusty Robotics's market positioning and traction align more closely with early-stage funding multiples or with the substantially elevated valuations of contemporaneous frontier robotics companies. Stage-progression analysis anchors a conservative floor; peer-median analysis may overweight later-stage or better-capitalized comparables. Additional clarity on revenue traction, customer commitments, and technology differentiation would be necessary to narrow this range materially.
